text:
mia: Quick async handoff from evening shift — few items:

1) SLO spike last night: 5m window ~ 6/1000 error rate on /v1/generate between 02:13-02:18 UTC. Root cause seems transient gRPC connection churn after a kernel update. Filed ticket #SRE-412.

devon: saw that. I muted noisy alert rule and opened a canary rollout to revert the kernel change on the affected pool. :thumbsup:

alex: PR up to change alerting window to 5m->10m for that rule to reduce noise: https://example.com/pr/334. PTAL @devon

jordan: oncall follow-up: is there any customer impact? Any retries/backoff needed?

mia: no customer-visible errors — requests retried fine. We hit higher 5xx counts in internal metrics but no 5xx spike in public latency SLO. Putting backstop fallback to smaller model variant if latency >2000ms.

sam: I left a note in the runbook (runbooks/kv-evict.md) with the rollback steps and the exact gcloud commands.

pagerduty-bot: Incident SRE-412 created by devon. Priority: P2. Links: https://pd/incident/412

devon: Also continuing with KV cache warmup patch, rolled to 20% canary. Monitoring token throughput and cache hit rate.

alex: quick CR ping: 2 small comments on ttl handling in patch — will push fix shortly.

jordan: blocker: the autoscaler didn't add new nodes during the spike for 8 mins. I'll follow up with eng-infra tomorrow, leaving an async ticket.

mia: today: finish SRE-412 triage, complete canary rollback if stable, update alert TTL and monitor for 24h. If anyone can review alex's CR — helps

devon: will take CR in 30m, and keep canary watch for 2h.

sam: I'll update the status channel and tag customers in the morning if rollback happens.

mia: thanks all — short and sweet. :coffee:

```
gcloud compute instances reset INSTANCE_NAME --zone=us-central1-a
```
